description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its Console “Rollouts” surface area to support route-level A/B testing with first-class measurement hooks (latency, cost, quality/eval scores) and safe operational controls. The project, Route-level A/B testing framework, adds the ability to define experiments at the request-routing layer (per route / endpoint / traffic policy), assign users deterministically to variants, and surface experiment health and results directly in Console.

Goals:
- Enable customers and internal teams to create route-level experiments (A/B/n) with deterministic assignment and configurable traffic splits.
- Provide measurement hooks and standardized metrics: latency (p50/p95/p99), cost/token economics, error rates, throughput, plus optional quality metrics from Redwood eval pipelines.
- Make experiments safe to operate: guardrails, automatic rollback triggers, audit logging of configuration changes, and clear blast-radius controls.
- Integrate with Redwood’s existing rollouts model lifecycle (canary, fallback policies) and policy engine.

Scope:
- Control plane: experiment configuration model (routes, variants, allocation, eligibility rules), validation, audit events, and API endpoints for Console.
- Data plane: routing policy evaluation changes to apply experiment assignment consistently (including stickiness keys and fallback behavior).
- Telemetry: define an experiment attribution schema and emit/aggregate metrics by {route, experiment_id, variant}.
- Console: UI to create/manage experiments, view guardrails, and visualize metrics and results; permissions aligned with RBAC.
- Applied ML: optional integration to attach eval scores (prompt set quality signals) to variants and to support “quality regression” alerts.

Out of scope (initial release):
- Fully automated experiment analysis (statistical significance engine) beyond basic deltas and guardrail thresholds.
- Multi-region cross-population rebalancing beyond deterministic bucketing.
- Customer-managed custom metrics ingestion (limited to Redwood-defined metrics + Redwood eval signals).

Stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts).
- Engineering (Console & Tooling): Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams.
- Platform Control Plane / Policy Engine: Ethan Park, Jordan Lee.
- Telemetry & Analytics: Logan Wright, Caleb Johnson.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant.
- Applied ML / Evals: Dr. Maya Srinivasan, Jonas Weber, Selene Huang.
- Design: Tessa Morgan, Kenji Nakamura, Alicia Perez.
- Release coordination: Connor O’Brien.

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Phase 0 (Jan 2025): PRD + architecture/design; define assignment + telemetry schema; align SLO/guardrails.
- Phase 1 (Feb 2025): Control plane APIs + router integration behind feature flag; basic metrics attribution.
- Phase 2 (Mar 2025): Console workflow + dashboards; eval-score hook integration; beta with design partners.
- Phase 3 (Apr 2025): Hardening (SRE runbooks, alerts), RBAC/audit logging completeness; GA rollout.

files.description: PRD defining user personas (platform eng, ML eng), core workflows (create experiment, monitor, stop), guardrails, success metrics, and phased rollout (beta→GA) for route-level A/B testing in Console.

Console UX spec: experiment creation wizard, variant configuration, traffic split controls, guardrail thresholds, results view, and audit/change history UI; includes empty states and RBAC-aware affordances.
ADR covering deterministic assignment strategy (hashing, stickiness keys), handling missing identifiers, cross-region consistency, and constraints for reproducible routing decisions.

ADR defining the canonical attribution dimensions and event schema for experiment metrics (route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, model_id, region), and the minimal set of metrics emitted at request/token levels.

Runbook for debugging split anomalies (skewed allocation, sticky-key drift, cache issues), including queries/dashboards to inspect assignment decisions and attribution integrity.
SLOs and error budgets for experiment APIs and config propagation (staleness bounds, API availability), plus alerting policy and on-call expectations.
Spec for standard dashboards/alerts: per-variant latency/cost/error guardrails, config propagation lag, attribution drop rate, and ‘variant 0 traffic’ detection.
Design for attaching eval score streams to experiment variants (prompt-set execution, sampling strategy, score normalization), and defining quality regression guardrails.
Audit logging requirements for experiment lifecycle events (create/update/start/stop/delete), including fields required for enterprise compliance and retention expectations.
